q: Which term is being defined below?

Regional Planning — Planning for the society, present and future, that involves physical characteristics, topography, climate, geographical location, soil condition, existing bodies of water, natural and man-made ecology, economics growth, employment, political and social structure. (Source: p.81-82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Multiplier Effect — The process whereby one change sets in motion a sequence of events that result in decline or growth. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Greenfield Site — Undeveloped land in a city or rural area used for agriculture or landscape design, now considered for urban development. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Collective Farm — A farm in which a group of farmers pool their land, domestic animals, and agricultural implements, retaining as private property enough only for the members' own requirements. (Source: p.79-80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Zoning — A planning tool used to designate permitted land uses in specific areas, e.g. residential, commercial, industrial. (Source: p.83)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Shanty Town — A group of unplanned shelters constructed from cheap or waste materials (such as cardboard, wood, or cloth), commonly located on the outskirts of cities in poor countries or on derelict land. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Planned Unit Development (PUD) — A type of building development and regulatory process that is a large-scale project not required to follow standard zoning rules. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Industrial Estate — An area planned for industry, where space is available for large buildings and further expansion. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Decentralization — The dispersion of a population away from a central point. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Agriculture — The practice of farming, including the cultivation of the soil for raising crops and the raising of domesticated animals. (Source: p.79)

o: Town Planning (Urban Design or Settlement Planning)
n: Answer: D. Town Planning (Urban Design or Settlement Planning) — The technical and political process of managing the physical growth and land-use of a self-contained settlement, defined by statutory zoning. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Poverty Cycle (Development Trap) — A set of factors or events by which poverty, once started, is likely to continue unless there is outside intervention; often found in inner-city areas and shanty towns. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Land Use Planning — The process of managing land resources to meet urban, economic, and environmental goals. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Employment — The paid jobs that people do. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Business Park — A low-density office development often established by private companies on greenfield sites, tending to be located near motorway junctions with a high proportion of high-tech firms. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Urban Model — Simplified diagrams used by planners to explain how cities grow and how different land uses (like housing, factories, and shops) are arranged. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Resort Town — An urban settlement whose main function is to cater for tourism of one type or another. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Mixed-Use Development — Urban development that blends residential, commercial, cultural, and industrial uses. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Community Planning — A grassroots-oriented process focused on the social, economic, and physical well-being of a specific neighborhood or community of interest, defined by its high level of public participation. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Slum — An area of poor-quality housing, typically found in parts of the inner city in rich countries and older parts of cities in poor countries; densely populated with inadequate services. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Population — The number of people inhabiting a country, region, area, or town; population statistics are derived from registration of birth and death and from censuses. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Industrial Location — The place where industry is found; industries have traditionally located near their markets, raw materials, or sources of labour, generally choosing where they can make the most profit. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Demography — The study of population. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Aid — Money or resources given or lent on favourable terms to developing countries; short-term aid relieves emergencies like famine, while long-term aid promotes economic development. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Urban — Human settlements with high population density and a built environment consisting of infrastructure, residential, and commercial buildings. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Primate City — A city that is far the largest within a country or area, holding a larger proportion of population, economic activity, and social functions than other settlements in the area. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Linear Development — Also called Ribbon Development; housing that has grown up along a route such as a road. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Environment — The conditions affecting a particular organism, including physical surroundings, climate, and influences of other living organisms. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Central Business District (CBD) — The area of a town or city where most commercial activity is found, dominated by shops, offices, entertainment venues, and government buildings; characterized by high rent and rates, tall buildings, and chain stores. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Urban Planning — A comprehensive, large-scale system design for high-density environments, defined by the integration of complex infrastructure networks (transportation, water, power, and housing) within a city boundary. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Rural — Geographic areas located outside towns and cities, characterized by low population density and large open spaces, with primary economic activity typically centered on agriculture, forestry, or mining. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Overpopulation — Too many people for the resources available in an area (such as food, land, and water). (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Heavy Industry — Industry that processes large amounts of bulky raw materials, e.g. iron and steel industry, shipbuilding, etc. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Conservation — Action taken to protect and preserve the natural world, usually from pollution, over-exploration, and other harmful features of human activity. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Shading and Media Aguas — A passive design strategy using deep roof overhangs and window awnings so the building self-shades, preventing the building envelope from absorbing solar heat. (Source: p.79 (Building Design))

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Sphere of Influence — The area surrounding a settlement that is affected by the settlement's activities, which may be mapped using catchment areas, local-newspaper circulation, delivery areas, and public transport destinations. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Population Control — Measures taken by some governments to limit the growth of their countries' population by trying to reduce the birth rate. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Infrastructure — Facilities that service an industrial economy, e.g. roads, railways, telephones, energy and water supply. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Depressed Area — A region with substandard economic performance, perhaps due to a change in industrial structure, such as a decline in manufacturing industry. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Bid-Rent Theory — The assumption that land value and rent decrease as distance from the central business district increases. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Urbanization — The process whereby an increasing proportion of a region's population becomes concentrated in urban areas. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Public Housing — Government-funded housing provided to low-income families. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Market Town — A settlement with a permanent or periodic market that acts as a selling point for goods produced in the surrounding hinterlands. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Free Port — A port, or sometimes a zone within a port, where cargo may be accepted for handling, processing, and reshipment without the imposition of tariffs and taxes. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Central Place — A place, or service centre, to which people travel from the surrounding area (hinterland) to obtain various goods or services. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Urban Renewal — The adaptation of existing buildings in towns and cities to meet changes in economic, social, and environmental requirements rather than demolishing them; gentrification is one option for raising an area's social and economic status. (Source: p.82-83)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Rural Depopulation — The loss of people from remote country areas to cities; it is an effect of migration. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Pedestrianization — The process of removing vehicle traffic from a street or district and converting it for the exclusive use of people on foot or bicycles, to improve air quality, safety, and walkability. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Hinterland — Areas that are served by a port or settlement (the central place) and are included in its sphere of influence. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
o: Town Planning (Urban Design or Settlement Planning)
n: Answer: B. Core and Periphery — Areas with different degrees of economic development; core areas are where capital, infrastructure, and development are concentrated, while periphery areas lack these resources. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Accessibility — The ease with which a place may be reached; an area with high accessibility generally has a well-developed transport network and is centrally located or at a route centre. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Squatter — An illegal occupant of a building or land. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Population Density — The number of people living in each area, usually expressed as people per square kilometer, providing a useful means for comparing population distribution. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Industrialism — The type of technology that utilizes inanimate sources of energy for driving its tools and sources of energy to produce goods and services. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Dispersed Settlement — A settlement made up of buildings scattered over a wide area. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Birth Rate — The number of live births per 1000 of the population of an area over the period of a year. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Urban Blight — The physical 'symptom' of a declining city, referring to the visible deterioration of buildings and public spaces, characterized by abandoned structures, trash-accumulating lots, and disrepaired infrastructure, often lowering nearby property values. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Pull Factor — Any factor that tends to attract people to an area, such as higher wages, better housing, and better education opportunities. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Megacities — Massive urban metropolitan areas with a total population of more than 10 million people, often serving as primary economic and political hubs but facing challenges with housing, traffic, and waste management. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Gentrification — The process of transforming a lower-income neighborhood through investment and new residents, often displacing the original community. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. City — An important, or high-order, urban settlement. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Urban Sprawl — The outward spread of built-up areas caused by their expansion. (Source: p.83)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Settlement — A place where people live, varying in size from isolated dwellings to the largest cities. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Peasant — A country-dweller engaged in small-scale farming, normally owning or renting a small amount of land, aiming to be self-sufficient and sell surplus supplies locally. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Ideal Cities — A concept representing the architectural and philosophical quest to create a utopian environment that balances order, social harmony, and functionality. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: A. Counter Urbanization — The movement of people and employment away from urban areas to smaller towns and villages in a rural location, pushed by factors such as congestion, high land prices, and population pressure. (Source: p.80)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: C. Agribusiness — Commercial farming on an industrial scale, often financed by companies whose main interest lies outside agriculture (e.g. multi-national corporations); mechanized, large, highly structured, and reliant on chemicals. (Source: p.79)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: B. Technology — The tools and know-how, connected with the use of both tools and sources of energy, to produce goods and services. (Source: p.82)

q: Which term is being defined below?
n: Answer: D. Population Distribution — The location of people within an area. (Source: p.81)

q: Which term is being defined below?
